title: Option-dragging a layer leaves a copy behind
goal: Laying out three cards or a row of buttons means making copies. Today the only way is Duplicate in the Layer menu, which drops the copy exactly on top of the original so you still have to drag it off. Holding Option while you drag should leave the original where it was and carry a copy away, which is what Photoshop and every design tool do.
notes: Nothing in CanvasView mentions duplicate today: the word does not appear in the file, and the .option reads there are the corner-anchored resize (line 1540), the region move (1570) and the fill shortcut (2135). The layer drag begins in CanvasView and runs through EditorState drag preview plus the multi-drag path that landed 2026-09-03 (queue/audits/2026-09-03-multi-drag.json). Read the modifier at the moment the drag starts, not continuously, so letting go of Option mid-drag does not undo the copy. Duplicate already exists whole in EditorState.duplicateSelectedLayers (line 3030) including the naming rule and group placement, so the copy should go through the same code rather than a second one. Ships unflagged, the way shift-click to add and shift-sweep to add did; if the runner judges it needs a switch it goes in FeatureCatalog as a Next flag on by default.
acceptance: Holding Option and dragging a layer on the picture leaves the original in place and moves a new copy
It works over a multi-selection: everything picked is copied and the copies are what you are dragging
The copy and its move are one undo step, and undo leaves the document exactly as it was
A copy made inside a group or a screen lands in that same group, and a copy of a component is a copy that still follows its original
Option keeps its old meanings: resizing from a corner about the centre, and the region tools that already read it
Try it: draw a box, hold Option and drag it right, then pick both and Option-drag again
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task
